brief.topic: Real strength is self-control in anger
brief.audience: Muslims looking for a short, authentic reminder they can act on today

coreInsight: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6114, strength is measured by self-control when angry, not by overpowering others.

hooks.text: Who's the strongest person you know?
hooks.notes: Clear in two seconds; the source answers it right away.
Works better as a takeaway line.

selectionRationale: Most relevant and clearest at a glance; the quoted source pays it off immediately.

scenes.excerpt: The strong is not the one who overcomes the people by his strength, but the strong is the one who controls himself while in anger

scenes.onScreen: TRY THIS TODAY / When anger rises, pause first. / Notice it early: tight jaw, fast words · Delay your reply until you are calm · Say less than you planned to say

caption.opening: Real strength isn't winning the argument.
body: Sahih al-Bukhari 6114 measures strength by something most of us don't expect: controlling yourself when you are angry.

Try this today:
→ notice anger early
→ delay your reply until you are calm
→ say less than you planned
